hook.text: Spray a field with glyphosate — everything dies except the Roundup Ready crop. Weed control simplified.

buildup.text: The EPSPS gene from Agrobacterium resists glyphosate — inserted into soy, corn, canola, and cotton.

discovery.text: No-till farming became possible — herbicide-tolerant crops let farmers skip plowing, reducing soil erosion by 90%.

twist.text: Overreliance created superweeds — Palmer amaranth evolved glyphosate resistance and now infests millions of acres.

climax.text: Stacked traits combine multiple herbicide tolerances — rotating chemistries slows resistance evolution.

punchline.text: Kill the weeds, save the crop — but evolution always fights back.

quiz.question: What unintended consequence arose from widespread Roundup Ready crop adoption?
options: Crop yields decreased due to the inserted gene
Weeds evolved glyphosate resistance, creating superweeds
The herbicide contaminated all groundwater permanently
